title: Prompt Cache: Modular Attention Reuse for Low-Latency Inference
technique: precompute and store attention states of schema-defined prompt modules (PML), reuse them position-correctly across prompts (approximate: attention limited to each module)

optimized_metrics.evidence: precompute and store the attention states of frequently revisited prompt segments in memory, and reuse them when these segments appear in the prompt to reduce latency
optimized_metrics.locator: abstract (design statement; §1 'reduces time-to-first-token (TTFT) latency from 1.5x to 10x' is result)

optimized_metrics.evidence: all while maintaining output accuracy and without the need for model parameter modifications.

headline_claim.text: The improvements range from 8x for GPU-based inference to 60x for CPU-based inference, all while maintaining output accuracy

reported_metrics.where: Table 2 / §5.5 per-token memory overhead of cached modules (e.g. 1K-token module = ~180 MB Falcon 1B, ~2.5 GB Llama 70B)

metric_definitions.definition_quote: We use TTFT latency for comparison, which measures the time to generate the first token, as Prompt Cache and KV Cache have the same decoding latency after the first token.
metric_definitions.notes: Single-prompt latency, no queueing; the paper says decode latency is unchanged so only TTFT is reported.

metric_definitions.definition_quote: In essence, Prompt Cache diminishes the latency involved in producing the first token, or time-to-first-token (TTFT).
metric_definitions.notes: Contrast: GPU speedup range quoted as 1.5x-10x in intro vs 8x in abstract (abstract rounds across hardware/memory placement).

load_regime: batch=1 single prompt, per dataset (LongBench 4K-10K context), CPU and GPU
tradeoff_acknowledged: Memory overhead of storing precomputed attention states (e.g. 2.5 GB per 1K-token module on Llama 70B -> CPU memory only); host-to-device copy latency when modules live in CPU memory (GPU speedup 5-10x vs up to 10x); possible accuracy change since attention is limited per module.
hardware: RTX 4090, A40, A100; Intel i9-13900K and AMD Ryzen 9 7950X CPUs
workloads: LongBench (8 datasets for latency, 21 for accuracy), plus recommendation/personalization examples
extractor_notes: Purely TTFT (per-prompt, no load); throughput mentioned only as an implicit benefit (§3.4). Quality metric is LongBench task score. Abstract speedup '8x GPU' vs intro '1.5x to 10x'.
load_class_quote: Figure 4. CPU latency measurements: time-to-first-token (TTFT) (per-prompt LongBench evaluation; no request-rate or batch-size load stated)
